The graph of the linear function $g$ is shown. What is the y-intercept of the graph of $y = g(x)$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. The y-intercept of a graph is the point where the graph intersects the y-axis. The graph of $y = g(x)$ shown intersects the y-axis at the point $(0, 3)$. Therefore, the y-intercept of the graph of $y = g(x)$ is $(0, 3)$.
